conventions.convention: Interior n_F points from K− to K+; [g]=g−−g+ and {g}=(g−+g+)/2. Boundary jumps and averages are one-sided traces, with the outward normal.

The main setting has d≥2, finite matching shape-regular affine simplicial meshes, scalar real polynomials of fixed degree k≥1, constant symmetric cell coefficients with common bounds 0<λ≤Λ, h_F=diam(F), and γ>0. Boundary facets participate in the penalty.

The form domain D_h requires cellwise H1 regularity, L2 coefficient-flux divergence, and one-sided L2 normal fluxes characterized by the weak Green identity. Interior q_F is half the difference of the two outward normal fluxes; boundary q_F is the outward flux.

Sobolev spaces on a closed physical simplex mean spaces on its open interior. Physical trace transfer uses an orientation-preserving affine reference map, and the trace/Green results assume Countable Choice.
The interval examples use a separate one-dimensional extension with counting measure on point faces; their h_F is the common interval-cell length 1/2.

The L2 theorem has s∈(1/2,1]. For s=1 it assumes piecewise H2 dual regularity and matching value/normal-flux traces; for s<1 it explicitly assumes adjoint consistency. The augmented dual approximation estimate is a separate hypothesis in both branches.

load_bearing.statement: On D_h, a_h is the broken coefficient-gradient pairing minus the two symmetric flux-jump pairings plus γ times the h_F⁻¹-weighted jump pairing. The squared DG expression is the cell energy plus that jump penalty; the squared augmented expression adds Σ_F h_F‖q_F(v)‖².

Assume Countable Choice. On each nondegenerate physical simplex in dimension d≥2, scalar and vector W1,2 functions have bounded L2 facet traces, independent of the orientation-preserving reference map, satisfying ∫_K(u div G+∇u·G)=Σ_F∫_F(γ_Fu)(γ_FG)·n_K,F.

Assume Countable Choice and the stated SIPDG setting. Every v_h∈V_h^br satisfies Σ_F h_F‖q_F(v_h)‖²≤C_flux Σ_K∫_K A_K∇v_h·∇v_h, with C_flux depending only on d, k, σ, λ and Λ, uniformly in cell sizes.
Assume Countable Choice and the SIPDG setting with γ>0. For all v,w∈D_h, |a_h(v,w)|≤(2+2γ⁻¹ᐟ²)‖v‖DG,*‖w‖DG,*. The energy expression is also a seminorm on D_h.

Assume Countable Choice and the SIPDG setting. If u is cellwise H2, has matching interior value traces, zero boundary trace, matching interior normal coefficient fluxes, and satisfies −div(A_K∇u)=f cellwise with f∈L2(Ω), then a_h(u,w_h)=ℓ_h(w_h) for every w_h∈V_h^br.
Assume Countable Choice. On a finite matching simplicial mesh of a nonempty bounded polyhedral domain, with λ>0 and γ>0, the SIPDG energy expression is a norm on V_h^br.
Assume Countable Choice and the stated SIPDG setting. If γ≥4C_flux, then a_h(v_h,v_h)≥(1/2)‖v_h‖DG² for every v_h∈V_h^br. For every f∈L2(Ω), the finite-dimensional SIPDG system has a unique solution.

Assume Countable Choice and the SIPDG mesh/coefficient hypotheses. If e is cellwise H2 and z is a cellwise H2 dual solution with matching interior value traces, zero boundary trace, matching interior normal coefficient fluxes, and −div(A_K∇z)=e cellwise, then a_h(e,z)=‖e‖L2².
